newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists plan poll pact with Communists.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists plan poll pact with Communists.

text.p: Socialist leader Lionel Jospin said he would seek an electoral pact with the Communists on Tuesday, before next month's parliamentary poll, and that France's next government may include Communist ministers.
The leader of the country's biggest opposition force is due to meet Communist Party chief Robert Hue in an attempt to iron out differences over a planned single European currency, among others.
"It's an electoral accord, a text which if we succeed will express our way of tackling the election and the issues on which we agree, including criticism of the Right," Jospin told Europe 1 radio.
"It's a common declaration on the election, it's not an agreement for government. If we were to form a government, it would represent the various opinions of the Left," Jospin added.
Asked whether he planned to take Communists into government if the Socialists won the May 25-June 1 election, Jospin answered: "I don't think that is the problem.
"The only problem is that of government cohesion. If there were to be a left-wing government, it could only be formed if there was only one clear political stance, including on Europe," he said.

The Socialists are in favour of the Euro although they have set conditions and refused further austerity steps if these were needed to reach the strict budget deficit criterion for European monetary union. The Communists oppose a single currency and want a referendum on the issue.
